2026-27.label: 2026-27 · projected

dpm.source: DARKO Daily Plus-Minus by Kostya Medvedovsky (darko.app)

clusters.name: Lead creator
clusters.description: High usage and assist share with a balanced shot diet; guards and wings who run the offense (Brunson, Maxey, Durant).

clusters.name: Spacing wing
clusters.description: Moderate usage, low assist share, most shots from three (Camara, Knueppel, Miles Bridges).

clusters.name: Two-way connector
clusters.description: Low usage, some playmaking, highest steal rate and above-average rim attempts (Derrick White, Dyson Daniels, Anunoby).

clusters.name: Stretch big
clusters.description: Big-man rebounding and blocks with a real three-point share (Holmgren, Mobley, Myles Turner).

clusters.name: Interior hub
clusters.description: High usage and assist share, few threes, rim-heavy and strong defensive rebounding (Jokić, Sengun, Scottie Barnes).

clusters.name: Rim runner
clusters.description: Almost no threes, three in four shots at the rim, elite offensive rebounding and blocks (Gobert, Jarrett Allen, Zubac).

limitations: Current association observed at acquisition, not backdated to season start.
Listed measurements are not combine measurements; career rates excluded.

2026-27.credit: After the Wyman diagrams by @taylormetrics and Databallr's Roster Shapes. Player ratings: DARKO DPM.
limitations: Size is (DPM + 2.0)^2.2 x minutes per team game. It is descriptive, not a forecast, a team rating or a verdict; DPM is a model estimate under lineup confounding, not causal.
Projected rosters use 2025-26 minutes over 82 games; a roster whose minutes add up to more than 240 a game is scaled down to 240. No 2026-27 minute has been played.
Shape is an estimate of ease of fit: the mean league percentile of DPM, defensive DPM, three-point rate and inverse usage, in eight equal bands. Read it as a lean, not a stat.

Playoff-adjusted moves each player by his DARKO offensive DPM change across the playoffs he played, weighted by playoff games and shrunk by 10 games toward no change. Players without playoff games are not moved. It is a proxy for Databallr's adjustment and does not model playability.
Derived archetypes describe one season's statistical style, not a listed position.
Players without a DPM or minutes are unknown and never drawn as zero; team fills are lower bounds.
White is the gap to the box, a +17.4 team: what a perfect team would add, not cap space.
